title: file-pcapng: Display additional details in Block header
description:
For all blocks include the offset and length of the block in the
Block header. For Section Header Blocks, report section endianness
in the Block header. For Custom Blocks, report PEN info in the Block
header.

notes.body:
Without this patch the block headers display as:

```
% tshark -X read_format:"MIME Files Format" -V -r pocorgtfo21.pdf | grep '^    Block' 
    Block 1: Section Header Block 1
    Block 2: Custom Block which should not be copied
    Block 3: Interface Description Block 0
    Block 4: Enhanced Packet Block 1
    Block 5: Enhanced Packet Block 2
    Block 6: Enhanced Packet Block 3
    Block 7: Enhanced Packet Block 4
    Block 8: Enhanced Packet Block 5
    Block 9: Enhanced Packet Block 6
    Block 10: Custom Block which should not be copied
``` 

With this patch, when viewing a pcapng in file format, the block headers display as:

```
% tshark -X read_format:"MIME Files Format" -V -r pocorgtfo21.pdf | grep '^    Block' 
    Block 1: Offset: 0x00000000 (0), Length: 28, Section Header Block 1 (Little-endian)
    Block 2: Offset: 0x0000001c (28), Length: 64, Custom Block which should not be copied (PEN: 2084794192 (<Unknown>))
    Block 3: Offset: 0x0000005c (92), Length: 20, Interface Description Block 0
    Block 4: Offset: 0x00000070 (112), Length: 1548, Enhanced Packet Block 1
    Block 5: Offset: 0x0000067c (1660), Length: 1548, Enhanced Packet Block 2
    Block 6: Offset: 0x00000c88 (3208), Length: 1548, Enhanced Packet Block 3
    Block 7: Offset: 0x00001294 (4756), Length: 1548, Enhanced Packet Block 4
    Block 8: Offset: 0x000018a0 (6304), Length: 1188, Enhanced Packet Block 5
    Block 9: Offset: 0x00001d44 (7492), Length: 108, Enhanced Packet Block 6
    Block 10: Offset: 0x00001db0 (7600), Length: 63930592, Custom Block which should not be copied (PEN: 1330009159 (<Unknown>))
```

This allows one to more easily extract a specific block (for example let's examine Block 2 "Offset: 0x0000001c (28), Length: 64" from above).

First as a typical hex dump:

```
% xxd -s 0x0000001c -l 64 pocorgtfo21.pdf
0000001c: ad0b 0040 4000 0000 506f 437c 2550 4446  ...@@...PoC|%PDF
0000002c: 2d31 2e33 0a25 c2b5 c20a 0a31 2030 206f  -1.3.%.....1 0 o
0000003c: 626a 0a3c 3c2f 4c65 6e67 7468 2032 2030  bj.<</Length 2 0
0000004c: 2052 3e3e 0a73 7472 6561 6d0a 4000 0000   R>>.stream.@...
```

Next as a Postscript style continuous hex dump:

```
$ xxd -p -s 0x0000001c -l 64 pocorgtfo21.pdf
ad0b004040000000506f437c255044462d312e330a25c2b5c20a0a312030
206f626a0a3c3c2f4c656e6774682032203020523e3e0a73747265616d0a
40000000
```

The Postscript style hex dump can be easily converted back into a binary stream and then output to other tools for processing (in this case to the hexdump utility configured to dump four octets per line which is particularly useful when examining pcapng blocks.)

```
% xxd -p -s 0x0000001c -l 64 pocorgtfo21.pdf \
   | xxd -p -r \
   | LC_ALL=C hexdump -v -e '"%07.7_ax\t" 4/1 "%02x "' -e '"\t\|" "%_p"' -e '"\|\n"'
0000000	ad 0b 00 40	|...@|
0000004	40 00 00 00	|@...|
0000008	50 6f 43 7c	|PoC||
000000c	25 50 44 46	|%PDF|
0000010	2d 31 2e 33	|-1.3|
0000014	0a 25 c2 b5	|.%..|
0000018	c2 0a 0a 31	|...1|
000001c	20 30 20 6f	| 0 o|
0000020	62 6a 0a 3c	|bj.<|
0000024	3c 2f 4c 65	|</Le|
0000028	6e 67 74 68	|ngth|
000002c	20 32 20 30	| 2 0|
0000030	20 52 3e 3e	| R>>|
0000034	0a 73 74 72	|.str|
0000038	65 61 6d 0a	|eam.|
000003c	40 00 00 00	|@...|
```
